liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Eyes Of The World** (2 reviews): Listener calls it one of the best up-tempo versions they have heard recently; Jerry makes band and audience rise to a new level, with audible gasps [24][35]
- **Estimated Prophet** (1 review): Performance on Estimated Prophet cited as one of the most stellar ever heard [35]
- **Goodnight Irene** (1 review): Listener notes it was not the breakout performance the audience was hoping for [31]

## The recordings

- **gd1983-12-31.155215.5-1.tobin.flac1648** (recommended): source not stated; 24 songs; 183 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1983-12-31.164337.senn441.vita..miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 23 songs; 166 min [2]
- **gd1983-12-31.148208.fob.akg.d330bt.senn421.hecht.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 23 songs; 157 min [4]
- **gd1983-12-31.151339.fob.nak700.wagner.miller.clugston.flac2496**: source not stated; 23 songs; 168 min [6]
- **gd1983-12-31.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.96185.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 22 songs; 173 min; rated 3.88/5 by 8 [13]. Said about its sound: Performance described as lackluster, sounding like an albatross for the band; Sound described as about as clear as it gets for a soundboard recording [26][29]

## Around the show

- Civic Center described as a cavernous mass; New Year's shows considered an albatross after Oakland [26]
- Listener questions if Tchaikovsky's 1812 Overture was an orchestra or just a recording on PA [28]
- Sequence of Big Boss Man into Iko Iko and In The Midnight Hour noted as neat [33]
- Mickey Hart on drums/cowbell; Rick Danko on acoustic guitar/vocals; Maria Muldaur on vocals/tambourine [1]
- Third set rated five stars, while the other two sets are noted as not lacking [27]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1983-12-31.155215.5-1.tobin.flac1648**: transferred by 5.1 LPCM Surround Sound Mix (48k) by Kevin Tobin; source: 5.1 LPCM Surround Sound (48k) mixed in Adobe Audition CC 2014 [1]. Also: Mixed by archive.org user; FLAC conversion done on 10-JAN-2022 by Trader Little Helper [1]
- **gd1983-12-31.164337.senn441.vita..miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Jim Vita's Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 441 mics > Sony D5M (Maxell UDXLII-S) [2]. Also: Nakamichi 700 source supplies a 0:09 patch in Space; Sennheiser 421 supplies Brokedown Palace [2]
- **gd1983-12-31.148208.fob.akg.d330bt.senn421.hecht.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Chris Hecht; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Chris Hecht's Master Audience Cassettes; (2) AKG D330BT mics + (1) Sennheiser 421 > Fostex Mixer > Sony D5M [4]. Also: Shnid126610 Matrix source patches Tennessee Jed beginning and Drums > Space section [4]
- **gd1983-12-31.151339.fob.nak700.wagner.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Bob Wagner; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Bob Wagner's Master (FOB) Cassettes; Nakamichi 700 mics > Sony D5M [6]. Also: Sennheiser 421 source patches My Brother Esau beginning, Drums, and supplies Brokedown Palace [6]
- **gd1983-12-31.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.96185.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Joani Walker and Paul Scotton; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (Nakamichi 550/Maxell XLII-S90) [13]
